correctness.rationale: The L1 norm identity reduces the problem to an l1-direct sum of a non-atomic conditional-averaging block and rank-one atomic blocks. Finite atomic truncations give the approximation upper bound; disjoint-support test spaces give the matching Bernstein lower bound. The same disjoint l1 witnesses give the exact distances to compact, FSS and SS classes. Nuclear sufficiency is an explicit rank-one series, and finite block compression plus the trace lower bound gives the matching nuclear-norm lower bound.

originality.rationale: The 2013 and 2014 L1 compactness criteria are contradicted by the rank-one trivial-sigma-algebra example. The 2026 arXiv v1 L1 nuclearity criterion uses conditional averages of |u| and is contradicted by a purely atomic block example. No source was located giving the corrected all-k approximation/Bernstein profile, exact SS/FSS/compact distances, complemented l1 witness, or exact nuclear norm. Residual risk remains from older Banach-lattice representation literature.

value.rationale: The result repairs a persistent endpoint issue, supplies two reusable counterexample mechanisms, replaces average-based atomic data by the correct L-infinity block quantity, and simultaneously determines finite-rank approximation, compactness, strict singularity and nuclearity for the same class.
